questions.question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM for the underlined word.

My teacher is very __diligent__.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Idle**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"diligent"** means someone who is careful and conscientious in their work or duties. (परिश्रमी)

 
 
• **Example: **My teacher is very diligent in preparing lessons for us.
 
 
 
• **"Idle"** refers to someone who is avoiding work or being lazy. (आलसी)
 
 
• **Example: **He spent his idle hours watching TV and playing video games.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the opposite of **'diligent' **is **'idle'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Idle**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Skilful **(कुशल): Having or showing skill.

 
 
• **Example:** She is very skilful in playing the piano.
 
 
 
• **Hardworking **(मेहनती): Tending to work with energy and commitment.
 
 
• **Example: **The team is very hardworking and dedicated.
 
 
 
• **Kind** (दयालु): Having a friendly, generous, and considerate nature.
 
 
• **Example:** He is always kind to everyone he meets.

questions.question:
Change the following sentence into positive degree.
Ramesh is not stronger than Mahesh.

options.text: Mahesh is as strong as Ramesh.
Ramesh is as strong than Mahesh.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. Mahesh is as strong as Ramesh.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in the comparative degree: "Ramesh is not stronger than Mahesh."
 
• To change it into the positive degree, we need to remove the comparison and state the equality of strength between Ramesh and Mahesh.
 
• The positive degree structure to express equality is: **"as + adjective + as"**.

Correct sentence: *Mahesh is as strong as Ramesh*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Comparative Degree:**

 
 
• **Structure:** subject + is/are + comparative adjective + than + object.
 
• **Example:** Ramesh is stronger than Mahesh.
 
• **Usage: **Used to compare differences between two objects they modify (larger, smaller, faster, higher).
 
 
 
• **Superlative Degree:**
 
 
• **Structure: **subject + is/are + the + superlative adjective + in/of + group/place.
 
• **Example: **Ramesh is the strongest in the class.
 
• **Usage: **Used to describe an object which is at the upper or lower limit of a quality (the tallest, the smallest, the fastest, the highest).
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence.

Swati came here with the intent of __insulting me__.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' to insult me.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"with the intent of"** is more formally and commonly followed by a verb in its base form with the word **"to"**.

• Option 2, **"of insulting me"**, though grammatically correct, is less formal and less commonly used in comparison to **"to insult me"**.

• **Verb Patterns:**
 
 
• Verbs like **intend, aim, decide** are often followed by **"to" + base verb**.
 
• Example: She intends **to visit** her parents this weekend.
 
 
 
• **Prepositions:**
 
 
• Using the correct preposition is essential to convey the right meaning.
 
• Example: I apologize **for** the inconvenience (reason) vs. I apologize **to** you (direction).
 
 
</ul

__
 
• The given sentence is an example of the** positive degree of comparison**, which is used to compare one item with another without indicating the highest degree.
